principles: Only fix the real learning-consumption gap: DONE experience must become candidate material before activation can be evidence based.
Keep Proofbound host-neutral: seed/proposal/candidate logic lives in CLI core, not a Codex/Claude namespace.
Do not optimize arbitrarily; reuse existing lineage audit, observeDigest, proposal, and candidate approval boundaries.
Preserve evidence safety: DONE success alone is not helped, not gate evidence, and not runtime active guidance.
drivers: Users need to see new DONE story experience enter the playbook pipeline without manual historical hunting.
Existing seed flow has digest guards and candidate inertness, so extending source lineage is safer than adding a parallel pipeline.
Story 2 needs candidates to exist before exposure/outcome/activation can be proven.

options.name: extend-source-lineage-with-done-experience
pros: Reuses source_lineage_audit, playbook_seed_observe, proposal, and candidate approval commands.
Keeps dedup and canonical key checks in one place.
Maintains candidate-only boundary and no-helped safety.
cons: Requires adding a new source kind and focused tests across several files.
DONE experience without findings needs a synthetic but stable sourceFindingId convention.

options.name: write-candidates-directly-from-done-settlement
pros: Would make candidate count increase immediately after DONE.
Requires fewer CLI steps for the first demonstration.
cons: Risks treating DONE settlement as promotion evidence.
Creates a second path that is harder to dedup.

options.name: wait-for-historical-backfill-story
pros: Could process all old data in one broader pass.
Avoids changing current DONE seed semantics first.
cons: Does not solve new DONE stories continuously feeding candidates.
Would mix historical ingestion risk with current-story learning closure.
Leaves Story 2 without fresh candidate proof.

rationale: Extending source lineage is the smallest correctness fix that proves DONE experience enters candidate playbooks while preserving existing digest guards and inert candidate safety.

preMortem.scenario: DONE success is accidentally counted as helped.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation reuses done-settlement outcome rows as positive samples or writes helped during seeding.
preMortem.consequence: Unexposed candidates could become eligible for activation based on completion alone.
preMortem.mitigation: Add smoke assertions that DONE success alone creates no helped outcome and candidates remain inactive.

preMortem.trigger: done_experience canonicalSourceKey is unstable or proposal approval ignores represented canonical sources.
preMortem.consequence: One DONE story appears as multiple independent lessons, corrupting promotion statistics.
preMortem.mitigation: Use stable story-backed lineage and test repeated observe/propose/approve dedup behavior.

preMortem.scenario: Source filters or priority break existing historical seed behavior.
preMortem.trigger: Adding done_experience changes default priority ordering or unsupported-source validation unexpectedly.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep source kind addition additive, preserve existing priorities, and run playbook seed promotion smoke.

preMortem.scenario: Docs imply automatic activation was implemented in Story 1.
preMortem.trigger: Execution docs blur candidate generation with V2 activation.
preMortem.consequence: Operators expect playbooks to become active without exposure/outcome evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Document exact candidate-only boundary and reserve activation for Story 2.
